patients.summary: Data entry specialist who joins the practice at 35 with autoimmune hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 88 mcg. Gynecology later diagnoses primary ovarian insufficiency during an infertility evaluation, orthopedics diagnoses right carpal tunnel syndrome, and depression diagnosed in 2024 goes on to a slow, disappointing sertraline course with psychiatry.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

Dawn is a 35-year-old data entry specialist transferring care from another primary care office. No acute concerns today; she mostly wants someone she can reach.

History: Hypothyroidism diagnosed around 2014 at her old office, told it was autoimmune. Dose was adjusted a few times early on and has been levothyroxine 88 mcg every morning for years, TSH reportedly fine on it. Takes it on an empty stomach, coffee about 45 minutes later. No palpitations, heat or cold intolerance, change in bowel habits, hair or skin change.
Gyn: menses regular, about every 28 days, no heavy bleeding. Not using hormonal contraception. Last Pap at old office, she thinks 2019, normal.
No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. No supplements.
Allergies: none known to medications.
Family: mother has major depression. A maternal aunt has hypothyroid and went through menopause very early, around 34. Paternal grandmother had rheumatoid arthritis.
Social: married, lives with husband. Works full time doing data entry, mostly at a keyboard. Never smoker. A drink once or twice a month at most. No drug use. Walks, likes to cook.

ROS: negative except as above. Mood good. Sleeping fine.

Exam: Well-appearing, pleasant. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules palpated. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin without rash. Neuro grossly intact.
PHQ-9: 3.

Assessment and plan:
1. Hypothyroidism, autoimmune - stable by history. Continue levothyroxine 88 mcg. TSH today.
2. Health maintenance - baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. HIV and hep C screening once, she agrees. Requested old records for Pap date and vaccines. Flu shot next month when this year's supply comes in; she will book a nurse visit.

Follow up: annual physical in the spring, sooner as needed. Gave her the practice cell number for texts.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dawn, all of your labs from Tuesday came back normal. Thyroid level is right where it should be on the 88 mcg, so no change. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests and cholesterol all look good. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, and those don't need repeating unless something changes. Talk soon.

documents.body:
Prior primary care office, records released at patient request. 41 pages.

Summary of contents:
- Problem list: hypothyroidism, autoimmune thyroiditis. Diagnosed May 2014 when a screening TSH came back high; thyroid peroxidase antibodies positive at that time. Levothyroxine started and titrated over 2014-2015 to 88 mcg daily, unchanged since. Annual TSH values on file all within range on that dose.
- Medications: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical screening: Pap with HPV co-test 06/2019, negative for intraepithelial lesion, HPV negative.
- Immunizations: Tdap 06/2017. COVID-19 Moderna dose 1 03/2021, dose 2 04/2021 (patient-provided card copy). Influenza most years.
- No surgical history. No hospitalizations.

Filed to chart. Immunizations entered. Next Pap due 2024.

Doing well. Busy stretch at work, long days on the computer but no complaints about hands, neck or eyes. Takes levothyroxine faithfully. Periods regular. Sleeps ok. Mood good.

Exam: NAD. Vitals reviewed. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck supple, thyroid normal size and nontender. CV regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs CTA. Abdomen benign. Extremities warm, no swelling. Skin: no concerning lesions.

Impression:
- Healthy 35 y/o. Hypothyroidism stable, recheck TSH, refills sent.
- Pap/HPV last 2019, due 2024.
- Vaccines: Tdap good until 2027. Flu in the fall.
- Cholesterol normal last fall; no need to repeat this year.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit.

She and her husband started trying for a pregnancy last October. Cycles still like clockwork, every 28 days, normal flow. Wanted to be sure her thyroid is where it should be for conceiving. No other concerns.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg. NKDA. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: Comfortable. Vitals ok. HEENT clear. Thyroid smooth, not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft. No edema, no rash.

Plan:
- Hypothyroid: TSH today. If she does become pregnant she should message right away, the dose usually needs to go up early.
- Preconception: discussed that at 36 it's reasonable to get a fertility evaluation if no pregnancy by 6 months of trying; that point is about now. She'd like to give it a couple more months first, will reach out.
- Pap due next year. Flu/COVID in the fall.

RTC 1 year.

Video visit on her lunch break, she is in her car, consented to video.

About 7 months trying to conceive without a pregnancy. Regular 28-day cycles, no spotting between, no pelvic pain. Husband is getting a semen analysis through his own doctor. TSH in March was normal.

Assessment: subfertility workup reasonable now given her age.
Plan: referral to outside gynecology for evaluation; they can do the hormone testing and decide on anything further. Continue levothyroxine. She'll let me know when she hears from them.

conditions.label: Primary ovarian insufficiency
conditions.note: Hypergonadotropic picture with very low AMH; cycles still regular.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER
Visit date: June 14, 2023
Referred by: primary care physician

Thank you for sending Ms. Cote, 36, for evaluation of difficulty conceiving.

She and her husband have had unprotected intercourse for about 8 months without a pregnancy. Her menses come every 28 days and she has noticed no change in length of cycle or in flow. Her husband's semen analysis was normal. She has autoimmune hypothyroidism on levothyroxine and is otherwise well. Family history is notable for a maternal aunt with hypothyroidism who reached menopause at 34. Never smoker, rare alcohol. No known drug allergies.

Medications: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.

Exam: Vital signs normal. Pelvic examination is normal, with a normal-size mobile uterus and no adnexal masses or tenderness.

Laboratory (drawn at this visit, resulted 6/16):
FSH 15 IU/L (3.5-12.5)
Estradiol 45 pg/mL (25-75)
Anti-Mullerian hormone 0.4 ng/mL (age reference 1-3)
TSH 2.5 uIU/mL (0.4-4.0)
Prolactin 14 ng/mL (4-23)

Impression: Elevated FSH with a markedly low AMH indicates a significantly reduced ovarian reserve. Taken together with the family history, this is consistent with primary ovarian insufficiency (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism), presenting before cycles have become irregular. Thyroid and prolactin are not contributing.

Plan: We reviewed what these numbers mean for her chances over time at 36 and that reserve is unlikely to improve. I offered referral to reproductive endocrinology for discussion of treatment options, which are time sensitive. She would like to talk it over with her husband before deciding and will call our office. Continue levothyroxine per primary care.

Gynecology

documents.title: Question about gyn letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I saw the gynecologist's letter posted. She explained it but I'm still kind of in shock. Does 'ovarian insufficiency' mean I'm going into menopause? My periods are totally normal. Not sure what to do about the fertility doctor yet.

documents.title: RE: Question about gyn letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dawn, I'm sorry, that's a lot to take in. It means your ovaries have fewer eggs left than expected for your age, which is why the gynecologist brought up the fertility specialist sooner rather than later. It doesn't mean your periods will stop right away; you're still cycling normally now. There is no wrong answer about the referral. If it would help to talk it through, book a visit or call me.

orders.reason: Right hand numbness and tingling, suspected median nerve entrapment

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: right hand numbness.

Since around April she's had numbness, tingling and a burning feeling in the right hand on and off. Worst at night, wakes her up most nights; shaking the hand out makes it go away for a while. No fall or injury. Left hand fine. No neck pain. Types all day at work.
Also updated me: she and her husband talked it over and decided not to go ahead with fertility treatment for now. She seems settled about it.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg. NKDA.

Exam: Right hand: Tinel sign positive at the wrist, Phalen positive. Radial pulse normal. Neck full range without pain. Left hand normal.

Assessment and plan:
1. Right hand paresthesias, likely carpal tunnel. Hypothyroid is a known risk factor; recheck TSH. Neutral night splint, sized here. Referral to orthopedics for evaluation and nerve testing.
2. Primary ovarian insufficiency per gynecology - no fertility treatment for now, her choice. Cycles still regular.

RTC after ortho visit or sooner.

documents.title: TSH result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Dawn, the doctor reviewed your thyroid test from Tuesday and it is normal, so no dose change. Orthopedics has your referral; their scheduler should call within a week or two.

conditions.label: Carpal tunnel syndrome
conditions.note: Right, median nerve distribution; thenar atrophy; prolonged median latency on NCS.

reports.text: Nerve conduction studies of the right upper limb, ordered by orthopedics for right hand numbness. Skin temperature maintained above 32 C. Right median nerve: prolonged latency across the wrist. Right ulnar nerve sensory and motor responses normal in latency, amplitude and conduction velocity. Needle examination was not performed.
reports.conclusion: Prolonged right median nerve latency at the wrist, consistent with median neuropathy at the wrist (carpal tunnel syndrome). Normal right ulnar study.

documents.title: Orthopedic hand consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
ORTHOPAEDIC SURGERY - HAND CLINIC
Consultation, October 19, 2023
Re: Dawn Cote, age 37
Referring: primary care

History: Six months of intermittent numbness, tingling and burning through the right hand, worse at night and frequently waking her. Relieved for a time by shaking the hand. No trauma. Background of autoimmune hypothyroidism and a recent gynecology diagnosis of primary ovarian insufficiency. Keyboard work full time.
Medications: levothyroxine. Allergies: none known.

Examination, right upper extremity: Visible thenar muscle atrophy. Tinel sign positive over the median nerve at the wrist. Phalen test reproduces symptoms at 60 seconds. Cervical spine range of motion full and painless. Left hand normal.

Studies: Nerve conduction testing today shows prolonged right median nerve latency (report attached).

Impression: Right carpal tunnel syndrome.

Plan: Given the thenar wasting, I recommended carpal tunnel release, and we went over the procedure and recovery time from keyboard work. She would prefer to keep using a night splint for now because of work and will call our office when she is ready to schedule. Advised her not to wait long if numbness becomes constant or weakness progresses.

Thank you for the referral.
Orthopaedic Surgery

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) given L deltoid and 2023-24 COVID (Pfizer) given R deltoid; avoided the right wrist side for comfort, she's wearing her splint. No complaints, no prior reactions. Monitored 15 minutes, fine.

documents.title: Hand update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hand surgeon wants to do the release. The splint does help, I'm waking up maybe twice a week instead of every night. Work is slammed until after the new year and I don't want to be out. Is it ok to wait?

documents.title: RE: Hand update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad the splint is helping. Waiting a bit is your call, but the surgeon recommended surgery because of the muscle thinning at the base of your thumb, and that part doesn't always come back if it goes on too long. Please don't put it off indefinitely, and call them sooner if the numbness becomes constant or you're dropping things.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical.

Interval: saw gyn in June (ovarian insufficiency, not pursuing fertility treatment) and ortho in October (right carpal tunnel, surgery recommended). Hasn't scheduled the release yet; splint most nights, hand wakes her now and then. Says she's been more tired than usual the last month or so, chalks it up to work and the winter. Periods still regular.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. NKDA.
PHQ-2 1.

Exam: Well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs without wheeze or crackles. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected. Right thenar eminence slightly flatter than left. No edema.

Plan:
- Hypothyroid: TSH. Refills.
- Tired: check CBC, CMP with the TSH; lipids while drawing.
- Carpal tunnel: encouraged her to follow through with ortho.
- POI: no treatment per gyn.
- Pap/HPV today.
- Up to date on Tdap; flu/COVID next fall.

RTC 1 year or sooner.

documents.title: Pap and lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Dawn: your Pap was normal and HPV was negative, so the next one isn't due for five years (2029). Thyroid, blood count, chemistries and cholesterol from last week were all normal too. If the tiredness doesn't lift with spring, let me know.

conditions.label: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chief complaint: tired, headaches, aching all over.

HPI: 38F with autoimmune hypothyroidism, POI, right CTS. Six months of fatigue, headaches and diffuse muscle aches that are now affecting her work (falling behind on entry quotas) and keeping up at home. When I asked more, she said she has felt down most days for months and isn't sleeping well. Feels hopeless about where things are going. Every so often thinks her family would be better off without her. Denies any plan or intent, has never acted on it, no firearms in the home. No prior depression treatment. Mother has had major depression.
No fever, weight change, rash, joint swelling, or new neuro symptoms. Headaches are dull, bilateral, no red flags.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg. NKDA. Alcohol rare.

Exam: Vitals normal. Flat but cooperative, tearful at times. Thyroid normal. Heart and lungs normal. No joint synovitis, no focal muscle tenderness. Neuro nonfocal.
PHQ-9 17, item 9 scored 1 (passive thoughts only).

Assessment and plan:
1. Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate. Likely explains much of the fatigue, aches and headaches; labs to be sure. Safety: passive SI, no plan or intent, protective factors husband and work. Made a safety plan together, gave her 988 and the practice number. Discussed treatment: therapy and/or an SSRI. She would rather not start medication right now and wants to try therapy first; referral to behavioral health placed. She knows she can change her mind about medication at any time.
2. Hypothyroidism - TSH, though it has been steady.
3. Labs: CBC, CMP, TSH.

RTC 4 weeks, sooner if worse. Asked her to text me in a week either way.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dawn, your blood count, chemistries and thyroid level all came back normal. That fits with what we talked about, that the tiredness and aches are part of the depression. Have you heard from the counseling office? How are you doing this week?

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thanks. Not great but I'm ok, nothing like what we talked about. They left a voicemail, I need to call them back.

Annual exam, age 38.

1. MDD, improving without treatment. Closing the unused behavioral health referral at her request. Low threshold to restart the conversation about sertraline if it slips. She agreed to message if PHQ-type symptoms come back.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Depression, recurrence of symptoms.

After the spring improvement her mood started slipping in June. Now low most days, anhedonic, tired, poor sleep, struggling to keep up at work. The thoughts that her family might be better off without her have come back a few times; no plan, no intent, no preparatory behavior. Wants to try medication now.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg. NKDA.
PHQ-9 16, item 9 = 1.

Exam: Vitals normal. Subdued, slowed speech, appropriate. Thyroid normal.

Assessment and plan:
MDD, symptoms back to moderate. Start sertraline 50 mg daily. Reviewed common early side effects (GI upset, sleep change, sexual side effects) and the 4-6 weeks it can take. Rare increase in suicidal thoughts early on - she will tell me right away. Safety plan updated, 988. Offered therapy again; she will think about it.
Recheck in about 6 weeks; plan to go up on the dose if tolerated.

F/u depression on sertraline 50 mg x 6 weeks.

Taking it daily, stomach settled. Mood maybe a little better on some days but overall not much different. Still tired and unmotivated, sleep broken. No thoughts of self-harm since the last visit. Using her safety plan card.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg, sertraline 50 mg. NKDA.
PHQ-9 14.

Exam: Vitals reviewed; weight up a couple of pounds from last year. Affect flat. Thyroid normal size. Heart RRR, lungs clear.

Assessment and plan:
1. MDD, small response on sertraline 50. Increase to 100 mg daily. Referral to psychiatry for co-management, given the slow course and her mother's history; she agreed to this one. Therapy still on the table.
2. Fatigue persists - CBC, CMP, TSH and B12 today.
3. Hypothyroidism stable.
4. Flu shot today.

Psychiatry wait is usually 2-3 months. Message me in 2-3 weeks on how the higher dose is going. Follow-up visit after psychiatry.

documents.title: Psychiatric evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PSYCHIATRY - NEW PATIENT EVALUATION
Seen December 22, 2025. Copy to referring primary care physician.

Identifying information: 39-year-old married woman, data entry specialist, referred for depression first diagnosed by her PCP in August 2024. Comorbid autoimmune hypothyroidism and primary ovarian insufficiency.

History of present illness: Her PCP started sertraline 50 mg in August and increased it to 100 mg about three months ago; she has noticed little benefit. For the past six weeks her mood has been persistently low. She wakes around 4 a.m. daily and cannot get back to sleep, and her concentration is poor. Activities she used to love, hiking and cooking in particular, hold no interest. Appetite is poor and she has lost roughly 10 lb unintentionally in the past month. She feels guilty for being unproductive. At times she wonders whether her family would be better off without her; she denies intent or plan. No history of manic or psychotic symptoms. She has never seen a psychiatrist or therapist. She says she would be open to therapy if it would help, but right now she feels too exhausted to search for a therapist or commit to weekly sessions. She denies recent psychosocial stressors. She asked whether there was something she could take to take the edge off so she can function.

Psychiatric history: as above; no hospitalizations, no self-harm.
Family psychiatric history: mother with depression.
Substance use: drinks socially, denies drug use. Never smoker.
Medications: sertraline 100 mg daily, levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Vital signs within normal limits; general physical examination unremarkable.
Mental status: Tired-appearing woman with poor eye contact and psychomotor slowing. Speech soft, coherent. Mood "empty." Affect constricted. Thought process linear. Hopeless about the future, yet willing to try treatment. Passive death wish without intent or plan. No psychotic content. Insight and judgment fair.

Data reviewed: CBC, TSH, CMP and B12 from October 1 at her PCP's office, all normal.

Assessment: Major depressive disorder, current episode, with partial at best response to sertraline at 100 mg for about 12 weeks. Risk: chronic passive ideation, no intent, plan, or history of attempts; protective factors include marriage, employment and engagement in care. Overall acute risk low.

Plan:
1. Continue sertraline 100 mg daily for now to complete an adequate trial at this dose; we will reassess at follow-up and adjust then.
2. Regarding something to take the edge off: explained why I would not add a sedative such as a benzodiazepine for depression; she accepted this.
3. Psychotherapy: referral placed through our clinic's therapy program and a short list of in-network therapists provided; we will help with scheduling.
4. Safety plan reviewed and updated; crisis line information given.
5. Return in about 3 months, sooner by phone if needed.

Psychiatry

documents.title: Saw psychiatry
documents.author: patient

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PSYCHIATRY PROGRESS NOTE - copy to PCP
Visit: March 17, 2026

39-year-old woman with autoimmune hypothyroidism, primary ovarian insufficiency and right carpal tunnel syndrome, followed for major depressive disorder first diagnosed in August 2024 and evaluated here in December 2025.

Interval: Now three months on sertraline 100 mg daily without meaningful improvement. Concentration at work is poor and she takes pleasure in little. Appetite down; she estimates about 5 kg lost over the past 3 months. Denies thoughts of harming herself. New concern: since starting sertraline her libido has dropped markedly, and it is causing tension with her husband. She has had one intake with a therapist through our program.

Substances: no tobacco, alcohol or drugs; she has not been drinking at all lately.
Medications: sertraline 100 mg daily, levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. NKDA.

Exam: general examination normal.
Mental status: low mood, constricted affect, linear thought, no SI, no psychosis.

Labs (drawn through our office this month): CBC, TSH and fasting glucose within normal limits.

Assessment: MDD, current episode not responding to sertraline 100 mg; sexual side effect.

Plan: Discussed options. Because she has not yet had a trial at a higher dose, we agreed to increase sertraline to 150 mg daily, knowing sexual side effects may not improve; if they become intolerable we will change course. Continue therapy. Safety plan current. Follow up in about 3 months.

Psychiatry

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PSYCHIATRY PROGRESS NOTE - copy to PCP
Visit: June 12, 2026

Follow-up for treatment-resistant depression, after evaluations here in December 2025 and March 2026. Background of primary ovarian insufficiency and autoimmune hypothyroidism.

Interval: Six months now of persistent sadness, loss of interest and fatigue, with no improvement in mood since the increase to sertraline 150 mg in March. She is distressed by significant weight gain and a further fall in libido, both worse since the dose went up.

Medications: sertraline 150 mg daily, levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. NKDA. No substance use.

Exam: BMI 32 kg/m2. Appears lethargic; otherwise unremarkable.
Mental status: dysphoric, constricted, no SI, no psychosis.

Labs (through our office): TSH and comprehensive metabolic panel within normal limits.

Assessment: MDD without response to sertraline at 100 and 150 mg; weight gain and sexual dysfunction on sertraline.

Plan: Reviewed options: continue as is, switch to a different antidepressant, or add a second medication. She wants to talk it over with her husband before deciding. Continue sertraline 150 mg for now. Continue therapy. She will call or message our office with her decision; otherwise follow up in about 3 months. Safety plan reviewed.

Psychiatry
